item.title: A least-squares lower bound for capacity
item.description: arXiv:2610.24702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a least-squares lower bound for the logarithmic capacity of an arbitrary compact plane set, extending an inequality previously known for connected sets. The bound generalizes classical inequalities involving area and moment of inertia. It is sharp for disks, and asymptotically sharp for compact sets whose capacity coincides with that of their interior. We further show that asymptotic sharpness holds for general compact sets if we replace logarithmic capacity by minimal carrier capacity.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Ransford

item.title: Semi-classical Szeg\H{o} kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.25255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $\Pi_{k,\leq k\mu_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, k\mu_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_k$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq k\delta)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.
item.dc:creator: Chin-Yu Hsiao, Chin Jui Yang

item.title: Pseudoconvex Exhaustions of Hartogs Domains Associated with $L^2$-Optimal Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.25294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By constructing a smooth pseudoconvex exhaustion of the associated Hartogs domain, we give a new proof of the Deng-Ning-Wang's characterization of plurisubharmonic functions without the smoothness assumption.
item.dc:creator: Xujun Zhang

item.title: Non-abelian LVM manifolds}
item.description: arXiv:2610.25368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the tangency construction of L\'opez de Medrano, Verjovsky and Meersseman from diagonal abelian actions to non-abelian Samelson groups. For these groups the tangency locus is a moment-map zero set: the commutator term in the leafwise Hessian vanishes there, and under an admissibility hypothesis, Kempf--Ness convexity gives a global transversal whose projectivization is a compact complex manifold. The construction includes compact rotation groups and groups with non-closed central rotations. In the latter setting we construct explicit families of complex dimension $2m-3$, $m\geq5$, which are $4$-connected and admit no symplectic form. Their meromorphic function fields are rational of transcendence degree $m-2$, although every holomorphic map to a projective space is constant. We compute their connected automorphism groups and show that they admit no maximal torus action. They are Hopf-surface bundles over compact complex quotients of stable Grassmannian loci; these bases give related examples already in complex dimension five. The families demonstrate that the non-abelian tangency construction reaches beyond compact complex manifolds with maximal torus actions.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Seade

item.title: Integrable distortion I: Weil--Petersson circle homeomorphisms and the Schoen conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.25580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A circle homeomorphism $\beta:\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}$ is Weil--Petersson if it has a quasiconformal disk extension whose Beltrami coefficient is square integrable for hyperbolic area. We minimise the hyperbolic anti-holomorphic energy \[ E_2(h)=\int_\mathbb{D}\eta(h)|h_{\bar w}|^2,dA, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \int_\mathbb{D}\frac{|\mu_f|^2}{1-|\mu_f|^2},dA_\eta,\quad f=h^{-1}, \] over all monotone Sobolev maps with boundary values $\beta$. For Weil--Petersson data, the unique minimiser is a real analytic hyperbolic harmonic diffeomorphism, globally quasiconformal and asymptotically conformal, with an explicit dilatation bound in terms of any admissible barrier's energy. We prove that a circle homeomorphism is Weil--Petersson if and only if it admits a finite-distortion homeomorphic extension satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}(\mathbb{K}_F-1),dA_\eta<\infty. \] For every $p>1$, the boundary values of a finite-distortion homeomorphism satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}|\mu_F|^p(1-|\mu_F|^2)^{-p_*/2},dA_\eta<\infty \] lie in Guo's $p$-integrable Teichm"uller space $T^p$. A capacity estimate for boundary moduli for the quasisymmetric ratio yields a derivative-free characterisation of $T^p$, essentially Bishop's theorem when $p=2$. The minimum defines a M"obius-invariant boundary energy, quantitatively comparable to the weighted square norm of the minimiser's Hopf differential. For arbitrary quasisymmetric data, we prove Markovi'c's theorem (the Schoen conjecture) by approximation with our smooth quadratic minimisers. Mori's theorem and the mean-value property of a logarithm verify the averaged-distance hypothesis in Riestenberg--Smillie's interior comparison, giving explicit displacement, energy-density and dilatation bounds in terms of the quasisymmetry constant. The nonquadratic ($p\neq2$) theory is developed in Part~II.
item.dc:creator: Gaven Martin, Cong Yao

item.title: An intrinsic notion of visibility and classification of planar Denjoy-Wolff domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.25815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we introduce an intrinsic notion of visibility with respect to the Kobayashi distance that does not require any boundary. We establish localization results for the Kobayashi distance on Kobayashi hyperbolic domains in $\mathbb{C}^d$ that satisfy this intrinsic visibility property. As an application of these localization results, we compare the Busemann horospheres of a domain with those of a subdomain. Recently, Benini and Bracci characterized simply connected planar domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property in terms of Busemann horospheres. More precisely, they proved that a proper simply connected planar domain has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of every Busemann horosphere meets the boundary of the domain in exactly one point. We introduce Condition (M$\star$), a condition of attaching a proper disk to the domain at a boundary point. Using our localization results together with this comparison of Busemann horospheres, we extend the characterization of Benini and Bracci to domains satisfying Condition (M$\star$) at every boundary point, and to domains satisfying it outside a totally disconnected subset of the boundary. In particular, we obtain a characterization for finitely connected domains and for a large class of infinitely connected domains having the Denjoy-Wolff property. These characterizations yield a variety of domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property, which we illustrate through example.
item.dc:creator: Nirmal Rawat, Amar Deep Sarkar

item.title: K\"ahler-Finsler rigidity of the Kobayashi metric and the K\"ahler base of weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a rigidity theorem: for every balanced, smooth, bounded pseudoconvex domain, its Kobayashi metric is a smooth, strongly pseudoconvex, K\"ahler-Finsler metric restricted on a neighborhood of the origin if and only if the domain is a Hermitian ellipsoid, biholomorphic to the unit ball. Thus for any balanced, smooth, bounded, strictly convex, and strongly pseudoconvex domain that is not biholomorphic to the unit ball, its Kobayashi metric is a non-K\"ahler-Finsler, weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metric. We also prove that the base manifold of every weak K\"ahler-Finsler metric is K\"ahler.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoshu Ge

item.title: On the group of automorphisms of the escaping sets of H\'{e}non maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.25891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we provide an explicit description of $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$, the group of automorphisms of the escaping set $I_H^+$ of a H\'enon map that induce the identity on its fundamental group. More precisely, for a H\'enon map $H(x,y)=(y,p(y)-\delta x),$ where $p$ is a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ and $\delta\neq 0$, we show that $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$ is completely determined by the degree and the coefficients of $p$. Thus, the automorphism group of the escaping set, subject to the prescribed topological constraint, can be explicitly characterized in terms of the underlying H\'enon map.
item.dc:creator: Mahima, Ratna Pal

item.title: Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Chu, Yaxiong Liu

item.title: Invertible non-cyclic functions in the little Bloch space
item.description: arXiv:2610.26318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a method for exhibiting functions $F$ in the little Bloch space $\B_0$ which are invertible, in the sense that $1/F$ also belongs to $\B_0$, and yet fail to be cyclic for the forward shift. The functions obtained in this way give rise to shift-invariant subspaces in $\B_0$ of index two, of a special type. The approach rests on a harmonic-measure criterion for non-cyclicity. This criterion gives a new manifestation of a principle of Borichev and Hedenmalm, and applies in a broad class of spaces of analytic functions.
item.dc:creator: Adem Limani

item.title: Invariance of logarithmic plurigenera and adjoint volumes in K\"ahler families
item.description: arXiv:2610.26519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider smooth proper families of compact complex manifolds over a disk whose total space is K\"ahler, together with a boundary divisor with relative simple normal crossings. We prove that, if the boundary is a rational divisor with coefficients in $[0,1)$, every logarithmic pluricanonical form on a fiber extends to a neighborhood of that fiber, and hence that the logarithmic plurigenera are constant. No positivity of the log canonical class is assumed. We prove further that, for real boundary coefficients in $[0,1]$, a log-adjoint class twisted by a smooth semipositive form has the same volume on every fiber, and that it is pseudoeffective either on every fiber or on none. When the log-adjoint class is nef on every fiber, we give a second proof of the extension theorem, which does not use the minimal model program.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

item.title: Two-parameter Toeplitz-type operators between Fock spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24318v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and study a two-parameter family of Toeplitz-type operators $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ on the Fock space $F^p(C)$ for $0<p\leq\infty$. For all $0<p, q \leq\infty$ we obtain sharp conditions for $\varphi$ such that $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^p(C)\to F^q(C)$ is bounded or compact. In the Hilbert space case $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^2(C)\to F^2(C)$, we also study the Berezin transform of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ and membership of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ in Schatten classes. Furthermore, we find a class of noncompact operators whose Berezin transforms nevertheless vanish at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Xingtang Dong, Zipeng Wang, Kehe Zhu

item.title: Asymptotics of Weighted Bergman Polynomials under Finite Regularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.24693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study strong asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials with respect to fixed weighted area measures on Jordan domains. The aim is to understand how the regularity of the domain and the weight enter the large-degree asymptotic behavior of these polynomials. For domains with real-analytic boundaries, Suetin established leading-order asymptotics for H\"older continuous weights, while Hedenmalm--Wennman obtained a full asymptotic expansion for real-analytic weights. We interpolate between these results while allowing both the boundary and the weight to have finite smoothness. The resulting expansions have a length determined by the available regularity and hold in the exterior region and, under sufficient regularity conditions, in a shrinking neighborhood of the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Lennart Aljoscha H\"ubner

item.title: Local Nevanlinna embedding for Hardy space of Dirichlet series below critical exponent
item.description: arXiv:2610.25002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a problem posed by Saksman and Seip [ Contemp. Math., 2016] on whether functions in the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $\mathcal{H}^p$, \(0<p<2\), are locally in the Nevanlinna class of the critical half-plane \(\mathbb C_{1/2}\). We show that the local Nevanlinna embedding fails below critical exponent \(p=2\) by constructing $\mathcal{H}^p$-functions whose local logarithmic mass becomes unbounded as \(\real s\to 1/2^+\). This also clarifies the distinction between global Jessen-type logarithmic control and local boundary Nevanlinna behavior for Dirichlet series.
item.dc:creator: Vasudevarao Allu, Dipon Kumar Mondal

item.title: Equidistribution, multipliers, and moving targets in polynomial families
item.description: arXiv:2610.25509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study equidistribution of parameters for each of which a polynomial has a cycle with a prescribed moving multiplier in the full critically marked or unicritical polynomial families of a given degree $d>1$. For the full critically marked monic polynomial family $f=(f_\lambda)$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$, of degree $d$, letting $p_{f,n}^*(\lambda,w)$ be the multiplier polynomial for cycles of formal exact period $n$ having multiplier $w$, we show that for any target sequence $w_n=d^na_n$ satisfying $n^{-1}\log|a_n|\to\ell\in[-\infty,+\infty)$, the averaged current of integration $\nu(n)^{-1}[p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)=0]$ along the zero divisor of $p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)$ tends to the $(1,1)$-current $\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^c\max\{L_d,\log d+\ell\}$ in the sense of currents on $\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$ as $n\to\infty$, where $L_d$ is the Lyapunov exponent function and $\nu(n)$ is the degree of the $n$th formal exact dynatomic polynomial associated to $f$. We also obtain the corresponding equidistribution theorem for the unicritical family $f_\lambda(z)=z^d+\lambda$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$, of degree $d$. The proof combines thermodynamic formalism, the Eremenko--Levin multiplier bound, and a comparison principle for plurisubharmonic functions, in a partly quantitative manner. A key ingredient is the vanishing of the bifurcation measure on the boundary of every component of the interior of the connectedness locus for the full critically marked family, which we show using Kiwi's study of critical portraits and rational laminations.
item.dc:creator: Y\^usuke Okuyama

item.title: Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances
item.description: arXiv:2610.25594v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: If a light source is sequentially lensed by $n$ intervening point-mass lenses at distinct distances, the number of isolated images for a generic source position cannot be greater than $2\cdot 3^{n-1}$. If lensing shear is present in each lens plane, the image counts could be as large as $4^n$, however. For a general multi-plane point-mass lens system, we also devise the recurrence for the BKK bound on the image counts, which is strictly less than Perry's bound due to the resultant degree for $n\ge 2$. None the less, this bound is still quadratic in the number of lenses on each plane, so is likely to overestimate the true sharp bound, which is expected to grow linearly with the number of lenses.
item.dc:creator: J. An (KASI)

item.title: Sharp Holder regularity for autonomous Beltrami equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.25702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$ be a domain and let $\mathcal H:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be Lipschitz with constant $0<k<1$. We prove that every weak $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solution of the autonomous Beltrami equation $f_{\bar z}=\mathcal H(f_z)$ belongs to $C^{1,\gamma}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, where $\gamma=3/(2K+1)$ and $K=(1+k)/(1-k)$. The exponent is optimal, resolving the conjecture of Astala, Clop, Faraco, J\"a\"askel\"ainen and Koski.
item.dc:creator: Jie Huang, Jian-Feng Zhu

item.title: A characterization of Griffiths semipositivity by top-degree optimal $\bar \partial$-estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.25900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on a vector bundle agrees almost everywhere with a Griffiths semipositive metric if its dual metric $h^*$ is locally integrable and the $\bar \partial$-equation admits solutions with optimal $L^2$-estimates for $(n,n)$-forms, where $n$ is the dimension of the base manifold. In particular, under this integrability assumption, Nakano semipositivity in the sense of optimal estimates implies Griffiths semipositivity.
item.dc:creator: Shin-ichi Matsumura

item.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26186v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001 and its generalization to orbifolds. Consequently, this establishes the expected equivalence between the \(A\) model (genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants with ambient insertions) of \(X\) and the \(B\) model (period integrals corresponding to vanishing cohomology) of \(X^{\vee}\) for Batyrev's mirror pair of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.
item.dc:creator: Tsung-Ju Lee

item.title: A proof of the Baranov--Bessonov--Kapustin conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin: for a non-constant inner function $\theta$, every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_\theta$ has a bounded symbol if and only if $\theta$ is one-component
item.dc:creator: Carlo Bellavita, Jani A. Virtanen

item.title: Symmetric Polynomials Method for the Multiple Loewner Chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.26716v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the technique of Symmetric Polynomials in the study of Loewner chains driven by a family of stochastic particle systems including but not limited to Dyson Brownian motion. As a first application of this technique we obtain the phase transitions at the critical parameter $\kappa=4$ in terms of the behavior of a class of symmetric polynomials evolving in time. We obtain new proofs of the phase transitions, we also obtain new closed-form expressions relevant for the models. In addition, we apply this method for some initial deterministic multiple Loewner evolutions. Finally, as this is, to our knowledge, the first paper analyzing this method in the context of multiple Loewner chains driven by root-system based multivariate processes, we also give an overview of potential future applications of this technique in the study of these models.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Andraus, Nicole Hufnagel, Jacek Ma{\l}ecki, Vlad Margarint

item.title: Functional Model for Isometric Pairs Satisfying an Automorphic Covariance Relation - I
item.description: arXiv:2610.26773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a canonical functional model for a pair of isometric operators $(V_1, V_2)$ acting on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ that satisfy the automorphic covariance relation $V_1 V_2 = V_2 \varphi(V_1)$, where $\varphi$ is an automorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. This extends the classical Bercovici--Douglas--Foias functional model for commuting isometric pairs to a dynamically twisted setting. When both $V_1$ and $V_2$ are pure isometries (shifts), the model simplifies to $(M_z, M_{\Theta} W_\varphi^*)$ acting on $H^2(\mathcal{F})$, where $W_\varphi$ is a unitary weighted composition operator on the Hardy space $H^2$ and $\Theta \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D}, \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{F}))$ is an operator-valued inner function such that $M_{\Theta}$ is a shift. As an application, we establish a complete unitary classification theorem for automorphically covariant isometric pairs by identifying a complete set of joint unitary invariants. Notably, our results are novel even in the special case of rotation automorphisms ($V_1 V_2 = q V_2 V_1$ with $|q| = 1$).
item.dc:creator: Sourav Ghosh, Haripada Sau

item.title: Subclass of bi-univalent function associated to Chebyshev polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2209.08300v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Chebyshev polynomials are utilized in this study to define the subclass of the bi-univalent function. Also, Chebyshev polynomial bounds and Fekete-Szego inequalities for functions defined in the classes are established.
item.dc:creator: G. M. Birajdar, N. D. Sangle

item.title: Levi Flat Structures via Structure Sheaves: Differential Complexes, Convexity, and Global Solvability
item.description: arXiv:2507.18341v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates Levi flat structures from the perspective of structure sheaves. We employ formal integrability to construct a class of differential complexes, thereby providing a resolution of the structure sheaf and a global realization of the Treves complex. Drawing inspiration from Morse theory and Grauert's convexity, we introduce notions of convexity and positivity that fully exploit Levi flatness, which yield global exactness of the differential complex and Sobolev regularity in the compact case. As applications, we establish the global solvability of the Treves complex for Levi flat structures, together with results on singular cohomology and the extension problem for canonical forms in the elliptic case.
item.dc:creator: Qingchun Ji, Jun Yao

item.title: Characterization of Asymptotically Smooth Chord-arc Curves
item.description: arXiv:2510.26514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an explicit example of an asymptotically conformal chord-arc curve that fails to be asymptotically smooth. This implies that a function belonging to both the little Bloch space and $\mathrm{BMOA}$ does not necessarily lie in $\mathrm{VMOA}$, and that a strongly quasisymmetric homeomorphism which is symmetric is not necessarily strongly symmetric. We also provide a complete characterization of asymptotically smooth curves in terms of asymptotic conformality and uniform approximability.
item.dc:creator: Katsuhiko Matsuzaki, Fei Tao

item.title: Invariant metrics of model domains near pseudoconcave points
item.description: arXiv:2605.01972v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give precise estimates of some holomorphically invariant infinitesimal metrics near a pseudoconcave points in a wide family of ``model'' domains for that situation in $\mathbb C^2$. This extends to metrics (rather distances) the authors' previous results from arXiv:2503.19754 and also takes into account defining functions more general than just power functions.
item.dc:creator: Pascal J. Thomas, Nikolai Nikolov

item.title: A Local Approximation Characterization of Oka Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10475v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the local approximation propert (LAP) and prove that it characterizes Oka manifolds. We prove that LAP yields convex approximation and, in an $n$-dimensional target, propagates across sets of zero $(2n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Consequently, strong dominability characterizes Oka manifolds, convex approximation in the target dimension suffices, the Oka property is local in the Euclidean topology, and it descends under surjective holomorphic maps. Local families of entire curves give geometric applications: smooth projective rationally connected manifolds are Oka, and deleting an algebraic subset of codimension at least two from any such manifold preserves the Oka property. Structure theorems further show that compact K\"ahler manifolds with nonnegative holomorphic sectional curvature or nef tangent bundle are Oka. Finally, the complement of a smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^n$ is Oka exactly when $d\leq n+1$.
item.dc:creator: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Oka manifolds are ubiquitous
item.description: arXiv:2610.10493v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a holomorphic family of connected complex Lie groups has Oka total space if and only if its base is Oka. Extension presentations and generating sections give Oka results for stable and parabolic bundle moduli and for holomorphic mapping and embedding spaces. Every nonempty degree component of maps from a compact Oka curve to projective space is Oka; rational-function spaces are also holomorphically elliptic. For a vector bundle on a smooth projective curve, the Oka property of its nested Quot scheme is equivalent to that of the symmetric powers determined by the length increments. Complete Hamiltonian flows give holomorphic ellipticity of irreducible \(\mathrm{SL}_2\)- and \(\mathrm{GL}_2\)-character and representation loci, for closed surfaces of genus at least two and for surfaces with fixed regular semisimple boundary classes. The Riemann--Hilbert correspondence yields Oka moduli spaces of nonresonant parabolic connections for arbitrary parabolic weights, and holomorphic ellipticity when reducible monodromy is absent. A proper holomorphic fibration over a Riemann surface, with a section and connected complex tori as smooth general fibres, has Oka total space exactly when its base is Oka. For a Schoen fibre product \(X\) of rational elliptic surfaces with disjoint singular values, we construct an entire local biholomorphism \(\mathbb C^3\to X\) whose image contains a dense Zariski-open subset. Further applications treat Hilbert schemes, compactified relative Jacobians, and logarithmic complements.
item.dc:creator: Sicheng An, Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Oka complements in algebraic tori and their logarithmic covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.15433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $K\subset\C^n$ is compact and polynomially convex. Write $q(z)=(e^{-iz_1},\ldots,e^{-iz_n})$, $X_K=(\C^*)^n\setminus(K\cap(\C^*)^n)$, and $Y_K=\C^n\setminus q^{-1}(K)$. We prove that $X_K$ and its logarithmic covering $Y_K$ are Oka. More strongly, $Y_K$ admits normalized holomorphic families of entire embeddings through prescribed holomorphic sections. The proof combines polynomial pair Hamiltonian transport in multiplicative coordinates, compatible with the coordinate hyperplanes, with a fixed Fatou--Bieberbach model. Applications include Oka slab crosses over arbitrary nonempty connected planar domains, complements of periodic equal-radius Euclidean balls centered at products of planar lattices, and complements of sufficiently small closed metric balls in products of elliptic curves.
item.dc:creator: Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Peng-Chao Wang, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: Pseudoconvex domains in complex Euclidean space with finite-dimensional Bergman spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$ such that the Bergman space is one-dimensional. Based on this example, for any integers $n \geq 3, d \geq 1$, we further construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that the Bergman space is $d$-dimensional. This disproves Wiegerinck's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yuan

item.title: On extremal problems related to the Krzy\.{z} conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23817v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study general extremal problems similar or closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture and establish the structural properties of extremal functions, pointing out some differences with the original Krzy\.z case. We also introduce a family of more specific problems of this kind, interpolating between the Krzy\.z problem and the problem of maximizing the constant term, and show that they are closely related to the Krzy\.z conjecture: the conjecture implies the analogous statement for all of them and, conversely, if one of them has the same extremal value as the Krzy\.z problem, then this value is $2/e$. This may represent a new approach to attacking the original problem. Finally, we show that for these problems an extremal function whose Taylor coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ vanish must be the conjectured one; as a special case, we obtain a new proof of a recent result of MacDonald.
item.dc:creator: Sarah May Instanes, Adri\'an Llinares, Dragan Vukoti\'c

item.title: Envelope of Holomorphy of Matsuki Orbits in Complex Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2509.17001v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the envelopes of holomorphy of Matsuki orbits $M_{\ell,m,r}$ arising as intersections of $G_0$- and $K$-orbits in complex Grassmannians. These orbits, equipped with natural CR-structures, form a class of compact homogeneous CR-submanifolds whose analytic continuation properties are of fundamental interest. Building on Rossi's theory of holomorphic extension, we establish that the envelope of holomorphy of each Matsuki orbit coincides biholomorphically with the containing $K$-orbit $O_{\ell,m}$. Our approach provides a geometric proof based on the holomorphic fiber bundle structure $\pi : M_{\ell,m,r} \to \mathrm{Gr}_{\ell}(E_+) \times \mathrm{Gr}_{m}(E_-)$, clarifying the role of compact isotropic fibers in constraining holomorphic extension. Explicit examples, including the orbit $M_{1,1,1} \subset \mathrm{Gr}_3(\mathbb{C}^8)$, illustrate the method and highlight connections with classical constructions in complex geometry and representation theory.
item.dc:creator: Irfan Ullah

item.title: A new $\nu$-metric computational example for the diffusion equation with boundary control and point observation
item.description: arXiv:2512.11428v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\nu$-metric used in robust control is computed for control systems with parametric uncertainty, governed by a diffusion equation in a bounded one-dimensional spatial region with boundary control and point observation.
item.dc:creator: Amol Sasane

item.title: Genus $2$ pencils on surfaces with $p_g=K^2=1$, envelopes, and conics tangent to plane cubic curves
item.description: arXiv:2603.03132v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider $(1,1)$-surfaces, namely, minimal compact complex surfaces $S$ with $p_g (S) =K_S^2=1$: for these the bicanonical map is a covering of degree $4$ of the plane $P^2$. And we answer a question posed by Meng Chen, whether they can contain a genus 2 pencil (this is the standard reason of failure of birationality of the bicanonical map). Our main theorem says that those which admit a genus 2 pencil form an irreducible subvariety of codimension $3$ in their moduli space $\frak M_{[1,1]}$; moreover, the general such surface admits exactly $24$ such pencils, corresponding to $12$ pencils of conics in $P^2$. The real fun is to relate this variety to the geometry of pencils of conics in the plane everywhere tangent to a cubic curve and a line. We investigate the corresponding variety $\cal{T}$ of triples and provide explicit equations using the classical theory of envelopes: among others, equations given in terms of the Weierstrass normal form of the cubic.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Catanese (Accademia dei Lincei), Noah Ruhland (Universit\"at Bayreuth)

item.title: Semialgebraic interior layers in root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2603.07397v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Finite-degree root plots of bounded-height monic integer polynomials can exhibit gaps around interior points of their root closures. Outside the closed unit disk, these closures coincide with Mandelbrot sets for affine iterated function systems with collinear digits. We construct explicit semialgebraic interior layers, certified when finite inverse orbits enter canonical self-covering parallelograms. Such parallelograms exist exactly in the non-real lens, which contains the non-real locus precisely from twenty maps onward. Within the non-real lens, limits of each capture level are captured within two additional steps, optimally, and the layers recover the locus by closure. The layers expose persistent interior deficits: explicit quadratic parameters evade every finite level; sufficiently close distinct parameters have logarithmically growing capture depths; the underlying lattice obstruction yields degree-dependent root-free radii, explaining such gaps. For non-real parameters of modulus at least the square root of the number of maps, exact enclosure trees have sharp, alphabet-independent branching bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule, David Juher

item.title: A problem for isolated singularities of surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.19452v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the extension of the conformal structure of a Riemann surface, obtained as a submanifold of $\mathbf R^n$, across an isolated singular point, under hypotheses that are metric rather than analytic. The main result (1989) is that an isolated singularity is $\textbf{conformally point-like}$ (conformal to a punctured disc) whenever it is $\textbf{$M$-regular}$: the pair (surface minus the point, the point) satisfies a Whitney condition, and the length of the spherical slice $S(0,r)\cap E$ decreases at most linearly in $r$, a condition described as ``metric decay''. This is proved via a modulus-of-rings (extremal-length) argument, generalizing the classical planar technique to submanifolds of $\mathbf R^n$. Two classes of examples are treated: surfaces of revolution generated by a single curve, and subanalytic surfaces, for which $M$-regularity is verified directly from Hironaka's structure theory, giving as a corollary that every isolated singularity of an orientable subanalytic surface is conformally point-like. A further original result is a $C^\infty$ counterexample showing that a strict Whitney condition alone does $\textbf{not}$ imply the linear length bound: the two hypotheses in the definition of $M$-regularity are independent.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Mosca

item.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2609.25762v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold admitting a strictly positive real $(1,1)$-current $T$ with smooth $dT$ and $dd^cT\le0$. We prove that the canonical bundle $K_X$ of $X$ is nef. If every positive Lelong level set of $T$ has complex dimension at most two, then $K_X$ is ample and $X$ admits a smooth plurinegative Hermitian metric. Strictly negative Chern holomorphic sectional curvature implies Brody hyperbolicity and, when constant, forces the given metric to be K\"ahler under the latter current hypotheses. We also establish K\"ahlerness for nonpositive constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature in Fujiki's class, and for nonzero constant curvature on compact complex threefolds and compact balanced fourfolds. In every complex dimension at least seven, we construct compact balanced metrics with zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature, nonzero Chern curvature, vanishing of all four Chern--Ricci contractions, and a nowhere-vanishing Chern-parallel holomorphic volume form. Finally, for compact Hermitian manifolds with zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature and vanishing first Chern--Ricci tensor, a smooth semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form, positive definite at one point, forces the metric to be K\"ahler flat.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin, Yuanhong Tian

item.title: The strong reproducing kernel thesis for Hankel operators and the Garsia norm
item.description: arXiv:2609.33242v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a bounded operator $T$ on $\mathcal H$, we say that $T$ obeys the strong reproducing kernel thesis (SRKT) if $\|T\|=\sup_k\|Tk\|$, where $k$ ranges over the normalized reproducing kernels in $\mathcal H$. Two problems are posed. One of these is to determine which Hankel operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ obey the SRKT. The other concerns the geometry of the unit ball of $BMO$ with respect to the Garsia norm.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin M. Dyakonov
